{
  "approach": "index",
  "change": "Add a composite index on the notes table to support the list_notes query pattern. Specifically, execute 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_notes_id ON notes(id);' (redundant but safe) and more importantly 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_notes_title_body ON notes(title, body);' to accelerate the LIKE searches for title and body. Since SQLite does not support functional indexes or full-text search natively in this simple setup, and the tags are stored as JSON text, we will rely on the existing sequential scan for tags but optimize the title/body search which is the most common filter. Additionally, ensure the connection is reused or opened once per request batch if possible, but the primary change is the index creation in initialize_db or a migration function called at startup.",
  "hypothesis": "The current profile shows significant time spent in sqlite3 execute calls, particularly for list_notes which performs full table scans for filtering. While previous attempts optimized the query structure, the lack of an index on the searchable columns (title, body) means every list_notes call with a search query still scans the entire table. Adding an index on (title, body) will allow SQLite to use an index scan for the LIKE queries, reducing the I/O and CPU cost of filtering, especially as the dataset grows. This should reduce the cumulative time in list_notes and the underlying execute calls.",
  "risks": [
    "SQLite LIKE queries with leading wildcards (%text%) cannot use B-tree indexes efficiently. The index on (title, body) will not help with 'LIKE %search%' patterns. This optimization may have negligible impact if the search pattern is always a substring.",
    "If the index is not used, it adds write overhead to INSERT/UPDATE operations.",
    "The tags filtering still relies on sequential scanning of the JSON text column, which remains unoptimized."
  ],
  "schema_version": 1,
  "used_memory": [
    1
  ]
}
